section: Landmark judgments - Maneka Gandhi, S.R. Bommai, Vishaka, Puttaswamy (privacy), Shreya Singhal, Navtej Johar, Shayara Bano

Recent Constitution Bench cases (electoral bonds, Article 370, SC sub-classification, demonetisation)

Judgments on AP matters (AP capital cases, AP reservation cases)

accepted.s: Which legislation was enacted in response to the Vishaka judgment of 1997?
o: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986
Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019
accepted.x: The Vishaka judgment led to the enactment of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013, commonly called the POSH Act.
accepted.tq: Link the landmark judgment to the legislation enacted in response.
accepted.sec: Case → law enacted in response (POSH Act 2013, Muslim Women Act 2019), earlier HC rulings on triple talaq

accepted.s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 was enacted in response to which judgment?
accepted.x: The Shayara Bano judgment was followed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019, which made instant triple talaq punishable.
accepted.tq: Use the case-to-statute association to distinguish closely related Muslim personal law cases.
accepted.sec: Case → law enacted in response (POSH Act 2013, Muslim Women Act 2019), earlier HC rulings on triple talaq

accepted.s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 was enacted following which case?
accepted.x: The 1986 Act followed the Shah Bano judgment of 1985.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named Shah Bano and Shayara Bano cases.
accepted.sec: Case → law enacted in response (POSH Act 2013, Muslim Women Act 2019), earlier HC rulings on triple talaq

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding earlier judicial rulings on triple talaq:
1. The Allahabad High Court held triple talaq illegal.
2. The Supreme Court dealt with triple talaq in Shamim Ara in 2002.
3. The Allahabad High Court ruling referred to in this context was delivered in 1985.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Allahabad High Court held triple talaq illegal, and the Supreme Court considered the issue in Shamim Ara in 2002. The cited Allahabad High Court ruling dates to 1994, not 1985.
accepted.tq: Check the precise year while retaining the correct court-case associations.
accepted.sec: Case → law enacted in response (POSH Act 2013, Muslim Women Act 2019), earlier HC rulings on triple talaq

accepted.s: Which of the following was struck down in the Joseph Shine judgment?
o: Section 66A of the Information Technology Act
accepted.x: Joseph Shine struck down Section 497 IPC, which dealt with adultery.
accepted.tq: Associate the judgment with the exact statutory provision rather than the broad subject.
accepted.sec: Case → law or section struck down or read down

accepted.s: Talaq-e-biddat was set aside by the Supreme Court in which case?
accepted.x: The Shayara Bano judgment of 2017 set aside talaq-e-biddat, commonly known as instant triple talaq.
accepted.tq: Use the specific form of talaq as the clue for the correct case.
accepted.sec: Case → law or section struck down or read down

accepted.s: With effect from 1 July 2024, which of the following correctly describes the position under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
o: The IPC continues unchanged and adultery remains an offence under Section 497.
The BNS replaced the IPC, contains no adultery offence and has no equivalent of Section 377 IPC.
The BNS replaced the IPC but retains Section 377 as a separate provision.
The BNS replaced the IPC and abolished the offence of bigamy.
accepted.x: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the IPC from 1 July 2024. It contains no adultery offence and has no equivalent of Section 377 IPC; bigamy is dealt with under Section 82 BNS.
accepted.tq: Separate the current statutory position from the earlier IPC provisions.
accepted.sec: Case → law or section struck down or read down

accepted.s: The Vishaka guidelines primarily dealt with which matter?
o: Registration of FIRs for cognizable offences
accepted.x: The Vishaka guidelines provided for workplace harassment committees and operated until the 2013 legislation was enacted.
accepted.tq: Match the subject matter of the guidelines with the originating case.
accepted.sec: Case → guidelines laid down (Vishaka, D.K. Basu, Prakash Singh, Lalita Kumari)

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the guidelines in D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal?
o: Informing a relative or friend of the arrested person
Constitution of a State Security Commission
accepted.x: D.K. Basu dealt with safeguards relating to arrest and custody, including an arrest memo, informing kin and medical checks. A State Security Commission was associated with police reforms in Prakash Singh.
accepted.tq: Find the guideline belonging to a neighbouring case rather than the arrest-and-custody case.
accepted.sec: Case → guidelines laid down (Vishaka, D.K. Basu, Prakash Singh, Lalita Kumari)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Vishaka — mandatory FIR for cognizable offences
accepted.x: Prakash Singh laid down police reform measures. Lalita Kumari concerned mandatory FIR registration, D.K. Basu concerned arrest and custody safeguards, and Vishaka concerned workplace harassment.
accepted.tq: Use subject-based elimination among four landmark guideline cases.
accepted.sec: Case → guidelines laid down (Vishaka, D.K. Basu, Prakash Singh, Lalita Kumari)

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the police reform measures associated with Prakash Singh?
o: Security of tenure for the Director General of Police
Mandatory registration of every cognizable offence as an FIR under Section 154 CrPC
accepted.x: Prakash Singh concerned police reforms including the State Security Commission, DGP tenure, Police Establishment Board and Complaints Authority. Mandatory FIR registration was laid down in Lalita Kumari.
accepted.tq: Identify the one guideline shifted from police reform to FIR registration.
accepted.sec: Case → guidelines laid down (Vishaka, D.K. Basu, Prakash Singh, Lalita Kumari)

accepted.s: The Lalita Kumari judgment held that registration of an FIR is mandatory in relation to which category of offences?
o: Only offences punishable with life imprisonment
accepted.x: Lalita Kumari made registration of an FIR mandatory for cognizable offences under Section 154 CrPC, now corresponding to Section 173 of the BNSS.
accepted.tq: Apply the exact legal classification instead of the broader term ‘all offences’.
accepted.sec: Case → guidelines laid down (Vishaka, D.K. Basu, Prakash Singh, Lalita Kumari)

accepted.s: Which provision of the BNSS corresponds to Section 154 of the CrPC in the context of FIR registration?
accepted.x: The FIR-registration provision corresponding to Section 154 CrPC is Section 173 of the BNSS.
accepted.tq: Test the transition from the old criminal procedure provision to the new provision.
accepted.sec: Case → guidelines laid down (Vishaka, D.K. Basu, Prakash Singh, Lalita Kumari)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constitution Bench decision on Article 370:
1. The Court held that Article 370 was temporary.
2. The Court held that the President could make Article 370 inoperative.
3. The Court directed that elections be held.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The December 2023 Article 370 judgment treated Article 370 as temporary, upheld the power of the President to make it inoperative and directed elections.
accepted.tq: Retain all three holdings of a Constitution Bench decision rather than selecting only the headline issue.
accepted.sec: Recent Constitution Bench cases (electoral bonds, Article 370, SC sub-classification, demonetisation)

accepted.s: The Supreme Court upheld demonetisation in January 2023 by what majority and under which provision?
o: 3:2 under Section 26(2) of the RBI Act
4:1 under Section 26(2) of the RBI Act
accepted.x: The demonetisation decision was upheld by a 4:1 majority under Section 26(2) of the RBI Act.
accepted.tq: Combine the majority figure with the exact statutory provision.
accepted.sec: Recent Constitution Bench cases (electoral bonds, Article 370, SC sub-classification, demonetisation)

accepted.s: The Supreme Court struck down the electoral bonds scheme primarily in relation to which constitutional right?
accepted.x: In February 2024, the Court unanimously struck down the electoral bonds scheme in the context of voters’ right to information.
accepted.tq: Connect the scheme with the constitutional transparency right identified in the judgment.
accepted.sec: Recent Constitution Bench cases (electoral bonds, Article 370, SC sub-classification, demonetisation)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Davinder Singh is correct?
o: A five-judge Bench unanimously prohibited sub-classification of Scheduled Castes.
A three-judge Bench permitted sub-classification only for Scheduled Tribes.
A nine-judge Bench by 4:1 upheld demonetisation.
A seven-judge Bench by 6:1 allowed sub-classification of Scheduled Castes and overruled Chinnaiah.
accepted.x: In August 2024, a seven-judge Bench in Davinder Singh, by 6:1, allowed sub-classification of Scheduled Castes and overruled E.V. Chinnaiah.
accepted.tq: Use bench size, majority and legal consequence together to reject mixed-up case descriptions.
accepted.sec: Recent Constitution Bench cases (electoral bonds, Article 370, SC sub-classification, demonetisation)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the bench size and Chief Justice associated with the case?
o: Vishaka — three judges, CJI J.S. Verma
Maneka Gandhi — five judges, CJI D.Y. Chandrachud
Electoral Bonds — nine judges, CJI J.S. Khehar
Shayara Bano — seven judges, CJI Dipak Misra
accepted.x: Vishaka was decided by a three-judge Bench headed by CJI J.S. Verma. Maneka Gandhi had seven judges, Electoral Bonds had five judges headed by CJI D.Y. Chandrachud, and Shayara Bano had five judges headed by CJI Dipak Misra.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive three-judge Vishaka combination and eliminate swapped bench details.
accepted.sec: Case → bench size and chief justice

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bommai — nine judges
2. Puttaswamy — nine judges, CJI J.S. Khehar
3. Maneka Gandhi — seven judges
4. Davinder Singh — seven judges
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Bommai and Puttaswamy were nine-judge cases; Puttaswamy was associated with CJI J.S. Khehar. Maneka Gandhi and Davinder Singh were decided by seven-judge Benches.
accepted.tq: Verify bench-size clusters before considering the Chief Justice detail.
accepted.sec: Case → bench size and chief justice

accepted.s: Which group of cases was associated with a five-judge Bench headed by CJI Dipak Misra?
o: Navtej Johar, Joseph Shine and Aadhaar
Bommai, Maneka Gandhi and Davinder Singh
Vishaka, Shayara Bano and D.K. Basu
accepted.x: Navtej Johar, Joseph Shine and Aadhaar were five-judge Bench cases associated with CJI Dipak Misra.
accepted.tq: Recognise the correct case cluster instead of matching a single isolated case.
accepted.sec: Case → bench size and chief justice

accepted.s: The judgment in E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2004) dealt with which issue?
o: It struck down Andhra Pradesh’s SC sub-categorisation Act, 2000.
It struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act.
It upheld 100% reservation for teachers in Scheduled Areas.
It upheld the electoral bonds scheme.
accepted.x: E.V. Chinnaiah struck down the Andhra Pradesh SC sub-categorisation Act, 2000. The decision was overruled by Davinder Singh in 2024.
accepted.tq: Associate the AP judgment with its precise reservation issue and outcome.
accepted.sec: Judgments on AP matters (AP capital cases, AP reservation cases)

accepted.s: Which case struck down the 100% reservation of posts for teachers in Scheduled Areas?
o: State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara
accepted.x: Chebrolu Leela Prasad Rao (2020) struck down the 100% ST quota for teachers in Scheduled Areas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two AP reservation cases by the reservation measure challenged.
accepted.sec: Judgments on AP matters (AP capital cases, AP reservation cases)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent legal position regarding the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Kurnool became the sole capital under the 2022 Andhra Pradesh High Court judgment.
Visakhapatnam became the sole capital with effect from 2 June 2024, and the Supreme Court approved three capitals.
Amaravati became the sole capital with effect from 2 June 2024, and Parliament passed the AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
The Andhra Pradesh High Court upheld the three-capital proposal in 2022 without legislative action thereafter.
accepted.x: After the Andhra Pradesh High Court’s 2022 ruling against three capitals, Amaravati became the sole capital from 2 June 2024. Parliament passed the AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, in April 2026.
accepted.tq: Track the sequence of court ruling, effective date and subsequent parliamentary action.
accepted.sec: Judgments on AP matters (AP capital cases, AP reservation cases)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. E.V. Chinnaiah judgment
B. Chebrolu Leela Prasad Rao judgment
C. Davinder Singh judgment
D. AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026
accepted.x: E.V. Chinnaiah was decided in 2004, Chebrolu Leela Prasad Rao in 2020, Davinder Singh in 2024 and the amendment Bill in 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the years as the first filter and then check the sequence of the AP developments.
accepted.sec: Judgments on AP matters (AP capital cases, AP reservation cases)

accepted.s: The public trust doctrine, as associated with M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath, means that:
o: Only Parliament can regulate private contracts.
The State holds natural resources in trust for the public.
The State may transfer all natural resources exclusively to private entities.
A law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights is permanently void in every situation.
accepted.x: Under the public trust doctrine, the State is treated as a trustee of natural resources for the benefit of the public.
accepted.tq: Apply the core meaning of the doctrine to the State’s relationship with natural resources.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: Which doctrine was laid down in Bhikaji Narain Dhakras (1955)?
accepted.x: The eclipse doctrine holds that a pre-Constitution law inconsistent with Fundamental Rights becomes dormant rather than dead and may revive if the constitutional impediment is removed.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive ‘dormant, not dead’ idea with its originating case.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: The doctrine of pith and substance is particularly relevant when determining whether:
o: A law’s true nature falls within the legislative competence of a particular List.
An invalid statutory provision can be separated from the rest of an Act.
A hazardous industry is liable without exceptions.
accepted.x: The doctrine of pith and substance examines the true nature and character of a law to determine its appropriate legislative List. It is associated with State of Bombay v. F.N. Balsara (1951).
accepted.tq: Apply the doctrine to a Union-State legislative competence dispute.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Colourable legislation — K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo
Prospective overruling — R.M.D.C. v. Union of India
Absolute liability — State of Bombay v. R.M.D.C.
accepted.x: The doctrine of colourable legislation is associated with K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953). Prospective overruling is associated with Golaknath, severability with R.M.D.C. v. Union of India, and absolute liability with M.C. Mehta’s Oleum gas leak case.
accepted.tq: Use the originating case rather than the definition alone to identify the correct pair.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: The principle that ‘what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly’ refers to which doctrine?
accepted.x: The doctrine of colourable legislation prevents a legislature from achieving indirectly what it lacks power to do directly. It is associated with K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo (1953).
accepted.tq: Recognise the standard formulation of the doctrine.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: Which case is associated with the doctrine of absolute liability for hazardous industries?
o: Motor General Traders v. State of Andhra Pradesh
M.C. Mehta, Oleum gas leak case
accepted.x: The absolute liability principle was evolved in M.C. Mehta’s 1987 Oleum gas leak case. It imposes liability on hazardous industries without the exceptions available under strict liability.
accepted.tq: Distinguish absolute liability from public trust and severability by the underlying subject.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: What is the essential meaning of prospective overruling?
o: A new judicial ruling operates only for the future.
A pre-Constitution law is dormant but not dead.
The invalid portion of a statute is removed while the remainder survives.
The true nature of a law determines its legislative List.
accepted.x: Prospective overruling means that the new judicial ruling operates prospectively rather than disturbing all past transactions. It is associated with Golaknath (1967).
accepted.tq: Match the temporal effect of the judgment with the doctrine’s exact meaning.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: Under the doctrine of severability, what is the effect of an invalid part of a statute?
o: The entire statute is automatically repealed.
The statute becomes dormant and automatically revives.
The invalid part is struck down while the remainder may survive.
The State legislature loses all legislative competence.
accepted.x: The doctrine of severability permits the invalid portion of a law to be struck down while the valid remainder survives, where separation is possible. It is associated with R.M.D.C. v. Union of India (1957).
accepted.tq: Test the practical consequence of severing an unconstitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: The doctrine of territorial nexus permits a State law to operate outside the State when:
o: The law concerns only Union subjects.
The law has been approved by every State legislature.
The law is immune from judicial review.
There is a sufficient connection between the State and the subject of the law.
accepted.x: A State law may have extra-territorial operation when a sufficient territorial nexus exists between the State and the subject matter. The doctrine is associated with State of Bombay v. R.M.D.C. (1957).
accepted.tq: Apply the nexus requirement to an extra-territorial State law.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case

accepted.s: Which doctrine is most directly applicable when a law enacted by one legislature appears to encroach upon a subject in another legislative List?
accepted.x: Pith and substance is the relevant doctrine for examining Union-State List encroachment by looking at the true nature and character of the law.
accepted.tq: Identify the doctrine from the federal legislative competence scenario.
accepted.sec: Doctrines → originating case
